  3055      OPM is consolidating Sec.  351.701(b) and (c), simplifying the 
  3056  method of applying assignment rights. Based on the new method of 
  3057  defining tenure groups and assigning retention standing based on 
  3058  performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference, with tenure 
  3059  subgroup and length of service as tiebreakers, subgroups will no longer 
  3060  play a predominant role in determining retention standing, and thus 
  3061  there is no longer a need for the separate concepts of an employee 
  3062  ``bumping'' another employee in a lower subgroup, and ``retreating'' to 
  3063  the position of a lower-ranked employee in the same subgroup. Instead, 
  3064  a released employee will have assignment rights to a position held by 
  3065  another employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure 
  3066  group, who is not more than three grades below the position from which 
  3067  the employee was released, and for which the released employee is 
  3068  qualified, pursuant to the criteria set forth in Sec.  351.702 and 
  3069  Sec.  351.703. This reform will significantly simplify the process of 
  3070  applying assignment rights in a RIF, eliminating the need for 
  3071  successive rounds of bumping and retreating between and within 
  3072  different subgroups.
  3073      OPM is eliminating Sec.  351.701(d). With the new method of 
  3074  calculating retention standing implemented in this rulemaking, which 
  3075  emphasizes performance over tenure and length of service, OPM believes 
  3076  that this restriction on employees with a current annual performance 
  3077  rating of record of Level 2 from obtaining assignment to positions held 
  3078  by employees with a higher performance rating is no longer necessary. 
  3079  OPM did not receive significant adverse comment on the removal of this 
  3080  provision.
  3081      OPM is modifying Sec.  351.702(a)(4), pertaining to qualifications 
  3082  for assignment to a new position, to include language clarifying that 
  3083  in determining qualifications for reassignment an agency must use an 
  3084  assessment that allows for demonstration of job-related skills, 
  3085  abilities, knowledge, and competencies; is based on a job analysis; and 
  3086  does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination. 
  3087  Commenter 0687 supported this change, expressing ``appreciat[ion] that 
  3088  OPM has added a mechanism for agencies to utilize assessments to 
  3089  determine qualification for those assignments that is skills-based and 
  3090  consistent with merit principles in selection.''
  3091      On the other hand, Commenter 0685 expressed concern that the use of 
  3092  assessments would ``inject subjectivity into what has traditionally 
  3093  been a more mechanical qualification determination.'' OPM disagrees. 
  3094  The current rule provides that an employee is qualified for a position 
  3095  if the employee ``[h]as the capacity, adaptability, and special skills 
  3096  needed to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position without 
  3097  undue interruption,'' but provides no other guidance for making this 
  3098  determination, other than that an agency may consider ``recency of 
  3099  experience, when appropriate.'' OPM believes that the use of a 
  3100  validated assessment that allows for demonstration of job-related 
  3101  skills, abilities, knowledge, and competencies, such as a structured 
  3102  interview, structured resume review, or a work-related exercise, will 
  3103  reduce the subjectivity of making a qualifications determination, 
  3104  requiring that an employee demonstrate their job-related skills in a 
  3105  measured, objective fashion. In so doing, OPM is aligning qualification 
  3106  determinations for assignment in a RIF with otherwise-applicable merit-
  3107  based hiring practices required under E.O. 13932, E.O. 14171, the 
  3108  Chance to Compete Act of 2024 (Pub. L. 118-188), and the Merit Hiring 
  3109  Plan.\17\
  3110  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3111  
  3112      \17\ Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy & OPM, Merit 
  3113  Hiring Plan (May 29, 2025), https://www.opm.gov/chcoc/latest-memos/merit-hiring-plan.pdf.
  3114  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3115  
  3116      However, OPM recognizes that, in some circumstances, requiring a 
  3117  new assessment may be unnecessary where official records already show 
  3118  that the employee recently and successfully performed the same or 
  3119  substantially equivalent work. Thus, in the Final Rule, OPM is 
  3120  providing that an agency is not required to administer an assessment 
  3121  if, during the 5-year period ending on the date the employee receives a 
  3122  specific RIF notice, the employee occupied the same position, or a 
  3123  position at the same grade or pay level with substantially the same 
  3124  duties, occupational series, qualification requirements, and conditions 
  3125  of employment, and received a rating of record of Level 3, Fully 
  3126  Successful, or higher, or the equivalent, for performance of those 
  3127  duties. This provision is intended to reduce unnecessary assessments 
  3128  while preserving the requirement that assignment rights be based on the 
  3129  employee's ability to perform the work.
  3130      OPM is modifying current Sec.  351.705 Administrative assignment to 
  3131  eliminate references to optional agency flexibilities to allow 
  3132  employees with lower retention standing to displace an employee with 
  3133  higher standing in the same subgroup under certain circumstances. With 
  3134  the more merit-based and straightforward order of retention implemented 
  3135  in this rulemaking, there is no longer a need for these exceptions.
  3136      OPM is retaining, and renumbering, current Sec.  351.705(c), which 
  3137  provides that agencies may, at their discretion, provide competing 
  3138  employees in the excepted service with assignment rights to other 
  3139  positions under the same appointing authority on the same basis as 
  3140  assignment rights provided to competitive service employees under Sec.  
  3141  351.701.
  3142  
  3143  G. Part 351, Subpart H: Notice Provisions
  3144  
  3145      OPM is modifying Sec.  351.802(a) to include the introductory 
  3146  statement
  3147  
  3148  [[Page 49205]]
  3149  
  3150  ``Except as otherwise provided in this part, a specific written notice 
  3151  under Sec.  351.801 must include.'' During previous rulemakings, OPM 
  3152  appears to have inadvertently deleted the opening part of Sec.  
  3153  351.802(a), which previously read: ``The notice shall state 
  3154  specifically.'' Adding an introductory phrase to the beginning of Sec.  
  3155  351.802(a) does not change the substance of the required notice; it 
  3156  merely makes explicit what the heading and enumerated list already 
  3157  imply. It also tracks the notice requirement in Sec.  351.802(a) with 
  3158  the relevant statutory text in 5 U.S.C. 3502(d)(2), which provides that 
  3159  a RIF notice ``shall include'' the personnel action, effective date, 
  3160  procedures used to identify employees for release, the employee's 
  3161  relative ranking and how it was determined, and appeal or other rights. 
  3162  OPM is including the phrase ``Except as otherwise provided in this 
  3163  part'' to account for the modified notice provisions allowed under 
  3164  Sec.  351.605(b) when an entire competitive area is being abolished; 
  3165  under such circumstances, an agency need not include the information 
  3166  described in Sec.  351.802(a)(2) or (a)(4) because the agency is not 
  3167  required to build a retention register and must not apply assignment 
  3168  rights.
  3169      In the proposed rule, OPM proposed to modify Sec.  351.802(a)(2) to 
  3170  substitute ``veterans' status'' for ``subgroup,'' and to add references 
  3171  to notifying employees of their tenure group and subgroup. In this 
  3172  final rule, OPM is revising this to ``veterans' preference subgroup.'' 
  3173  OPM is also updating language in Sec.  351.802(a)(3) by requiring 
  3174  agencies to provide competing employees with a link to 5 CFR part 351 
  3175  and access to the agency's records pertinent to the RIF being run.
  3176      OPM is adopting a clarifying amendment to Sec.  351.805(b) to 
  3177  conform that provision to proposed Sec.  351.507. In the proposed rule, 
  3178  OPM proposed to determine retention standing as of the date the 
  3179  employee receives a specific reduction in force notice, rather than the 
  3180  date on which the RIF action is ultimately effected. OPM explained that 
  3181  this change is necessary because the actual effective date of a RIF 
  3182  action may be delayed by litigation or other unforeseen factors, and 
  3183  that requiring agencies to rerun retention registers whenever a RIF 
  3184  effective date is delayed would be costly and time-consuming.
  3185      Current Sec.  351.805(b) already requires an agency to issue an 
  3186  amended written notice if a RIF is changed to a later effective date. 
  3187  The amendment to Sec.  351.805(b) clarifies that an amended notice 
  3188  issued solely to state a later effective date is not a new specific 
  3189  reduction in force notice for purposes of Sec.  351.507 and does not 
  3190  require the agency to redetermine or recalculate retention standing 
  3191  under subpart E. This amendment confirms the necessary consequence of 
  3192  Sec.  351.507: once retention standing is fixed as of the date of the 
  3193  specific RIF notice, a ministerial amended notice delaying the 
  3194  effective date does not restart the retention-standing calculation. The 
  3195  amendment provides that it does not affect an agency's obligation to 
  3196  correct an error under Sec.  351.507(c).
  3197  
  3198  H. Part 316, Subpart I: Post-Secondary Student Hiring Authority
  3199  
  3200      OPM is revising Sec.  316.911, which specifies how RIF procedures 
  3201  apply to employees hired under the post-secondary student hiring 
  3202  authority under 5 U.S.C. 3116 and 5 CFR part 316, subpart I, to comport 
  3203  with the changes to part 351 that OPM is making elsewhere in this rule. 
  3204  OPM did not receive significant adverse comment regarding this change

content.text:
I'm checking the preamble against the final regulation text, and comparing the three-grades-below point with what the preamble says about 351.701(d). It looks like the preamble describes that paragraph as being eliminated, but in the final rule 351.701(d) contains new grade progression and pay band text.

Next I'm checking the preamble's wording on automated self-assessments against the regulation, which says "solely of, or principally rely on," while the preamble bans any reliance. I'm also confirming the renumbering of 351.705(c) to (a) and the veterans' preference and tenure subgroup references, which match.

I'm comparing the preamble's reference to 351.802 and the notice contents against the regulation, but I can't verify those without the 351.802 text. Next I'm reading the Part 330 section of the preamble, along with 353 and 430, since more mismatches are likely there.

[2026-15665: lines 3205-3419 of 6220, FR page 49205]
  3205  and is finalizing it.
  3206  
  3207  I. Part 330: RPL, ICTAP, and CTAP
  3208  
  3209      OPM is making various changes to 5 CFR part 330 to conform the 
  3210  provisions of this part pertaining to RPL, ICTAP, and CTAP to the other 
  3211  changes made in this rulemaking, most notably the modifications to 
  3212  tenure groups I, II and III, and to update some of the terminology. 
  3213  RPL, ICTAP, and CTAP are designed to help employees who have been, or 
  3214  are about to be, displaced by a RIF find continued Federal employment, 
  3215  so part 330 needs to align with the revised RIF definitions and 
  3216  concepts in part 351. In the proposed rule, OPM stated expressly that 
  3217  it does not intend for the coverage definitions to apply retroactively 
  3218  in a way that would deprive employees who already received a RIF 
  3219  separation notice, declined a directed geographic reassignment, or 
  3220  received a notice of expected separation before the rule's effective 
  3221  date of eligibility for coverage; the rule adds coverage for ``another 
  3222  qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM'' to 
  3223  ensure that there are no gaps.
  3224      OPM is also making several changes to strengthen the merit basis 
  3225  for RPL, ICTAP and CTAP placement. For example, OPM is changing the 
  3226  definition of ``qualified'' in Sec.  330.202 to align with OPM's 
  3227  definition of that same term in Sec.  351.702 (in the context of 
  3228  assignment rights in a RIF). To be qualified for a position, an RPL 
  3229  registrant, just like an employee competing in a RIF, will be required 
  3230  to have the capacity, adaptability, and special skills necessary to 
  3231  satisfactorily perform the duties of the position, as demonstrated 
  3232  through a valid, job-related assessment. This change strengthens RPL 
  3233  placement by ensuring candidates are matched to jobs through real, job-
  3234  related assessment rather than paper or self-rated qualification 
  3235  screens.
  3236      OPM is also modifying Sec.  330.213(c), which prescribes a method 
  3237  for selecting qualified RPL placement priority candidates based on 
  3238  numerical scoring. Instead of rating and ranking candidates based on 
  3239  job experience and education, an agency using this method must instead 
  3240  rate and rank candidates based on their job-related skills, knowledge, 
  3241  and competencies as measured by an assessment. Agencies using the 
  3242  numerical scoring method will be required to rate and rank qualified 
  3243  RPL placement priority candidates in a fair and consistent manner, and 
  3244  will be required to assign additional points to candidates based on 
  3245  veterans' preference. This change maintains RPL priority but makes the 
  3246  selection process more skills-based and consistent with the revised RIF 
  3247  framework.
  3248      Commenter 0720, a Federal agency, supported these changes to 5 CFR 
  3249  part 330. It noted that the frameworks governing RPL, CTAP and ICTAP 
  3250  were developed decades ago, and the changes proposed by OPM would align 
  3251  these programs with the performance-forward retention model, improve 
  3252  clarity around eligibility and priority placement, and support more 
  3253  predictable reemployment outcomes for affected employees.
  3254      Some commenters (for example, 0037, 0125, 0317, and 0412) opposed 
  3255  these changes, believing that they would weaken RPL, CTAP, and ICTAP. 
  3256  OPM does not agree. The revisions in this rule preserve the core 
  3257  placement rights and selection priorities of RPL, CTAP, and ICTAP while 
  3258  aligning those programs with the revised part 351 RIF structure and 
  3259  improving the accuracy of qualification determinations. Under the 
  3260  revised RPL retention-standing method, the agency still must place 
  3261  qualified RPL candidates in retention-standing order and may not pass 
  3262  over a higher-standing candidate to select a lower-standing candidate. 
  3263  This rule does not eliminate the core CTAP rule that an agency may not 
  3264  place another candidate into a vacancy if an available CTAP selection-
  3265  priority candidate exists, unless a regulatory exception applies. And 
  3266  this rule retains the requirement that an agency may not appoint a 
  3267  candidate from outside its permanent competitive-service workforce into 
  3268  a vacancy if an ICTAP selection-priority candidate is available, unless 
  3269  an exception applies. Further, requiring job-analysis-based assessments 
  3270  that
  3271  
  3272  [[Page 49206]]
  3273  
  3274  measure job-related skills, abilities, knowledge, and competencies 
  3275  reduces overreliance on automated self-assessments and helps ensure RPL 
  3276  candidates are genuinely qualified for the vacancies into which 
  3277  agencies place them.
  3278      OPM is adopting its proposed changes to 5 CFR part 330 in this 
  3279  final rule, with one exception. OPM is not proceeding with adding 
  3280  finalizing the appointment of an employee serving a trial period under 
  3281  Civil Service Rule 11 to the lists of permitted personnel actions that 
  3282  may be taken as an exception to CTAP selection priority in Sec.  
  3283  330.609, and ICTAP selection priority in Sec.  330.707. It is not 
  3284  including these additions because CTAP and ICTAP only apply to filling 
  3285  vacancies in the competitive service, and trial periods under Civil 
  3286  Service Rule 11 apply only to excepted service employees. Thus, there 
  3287  is no need to identify finalizing an excepted service appointment as an 
  3288  exception to ICTAP and CTAP selection priority.
  3289  
  3290  J. Part 353: Retention Protections During Uniformed Service
  3291  
  3292      In this final rule, OPM is revising Sec.  353.110(a) to remove an 
  3293  outdated reference to the address where employees seeking OPM placement 
  3294  assistance in the executive branch must provide notice, and add the 
  3295  current, up-to-date email address. This technical amendment reflects 
  3296  OPM's current organizational routing and does not alter any substantive 
  3297  right or obligation.
  3298      Additionally, in this final rule, OPM is revising Sec.  353.301(b) 
  3299  to provide more information about how retention protections for 
  3300  individuals serving in the uniformed services operate during a RIF. OPM 
  3301  is making these changes in response to comments seeking more clarity on 
  3302  how USERRA protections operate during a RIF, and to ensure that 
  3303  restoration protections for employees absent because of uniformed 
  3304  service or compensable injury operate coherently with the final 
  3305  revisions to part 351.
  3306      Current Sec.  353.209(a) already provides that an employee 
  3307  performing duty with the uniformed services may not be demoted or 
  3308  separated, other than military separation, except for cause; that RIF 
  3309  is not ``for cause''; that such an employee is not a competing employee 
  3310  under part 351; and that, if the employee's position is abolished 
  3311  during the absence, the agency must reassign the employee to another 
  3312  position of like status and pay. This final rule clarifies that this 
  3313  reassignment obligation applies when the employee's position is 
  3314  abolished as part of the abolishment of an entire competitive area 
  3315  under Sec.  351.605. These additional edits clarify how restoration 
  3316  rights apply when an employee's position is abolished in connection 
  3317  with a RIF, including when an agency abolishes all positions in a 
  3318  competitive area under Sec.  351.605.
  3319      OPM is removing a reference to tenure group III in Sec.  
  3320  353.301(a). Instead of ``tenure group III,'' OPM is substituting 
  3321  ``temporary, term or indefinite appointment,'' which encompasses the 
  3322  categories previously included in tenure group III.
  3323  
  3324  K. Part 359: SES Furloughs
  3325  
  3326      Consistent with the changes to the definition of ``furlough'' in 
  3327  Sec.  351.203, OPM is revising the definition of ``furlough'' in Sec.  
  3328  359.802 (regulating furloughs in the SES) to align with OPM's 
  3329  longstanding guidance that SES competitive furlough requirements are 
  3330  not applicable to emergency shutdown furloughs due to a lapse in 
  3331  appropriations where the ultimate duration of the furlough is unknown 
  3332  at the outset. Commenter 0683 agreed that this change appropriately 
  3333  distinguishes between planned agency-initiated furloughs and emergency 
  3334  furloughs driven by congressional inaction. OPM did not receive 
  3335  significant adverse comment regarding this change and is finalizing it.
  3336  
  3337  L. Part 362: Pathways Programs
  3338  
  3339      OPM is modifying 5 CFR 362.205 regarding the Pathways Intern 
  3340  Program by removing references to how RIF procedures apply to Pathways 
  3341  interns, as those references would no longer be accurate or necessary 
  3342  given OPM's changes to Part 351. Pursuant to revised Sec.  351.502(b), 
  3343  the termination of a Pathways intern will only be covered by RIF 
  3344  procedures if the intern had completed a trial period under 5 CFR 11.3. 
  3345  Otherwise, Pathways interns could be retained or separated by an agency 
  3346  without regard to RIF procedures.
  3347      OPM is also revising Sec.  362.306(a) to conform the Recent 
  3348  Graduates Program regulation to the final revisions to part 351. 
  3349  Current Sec.  362.306(a) provides that Recent Graduates are in excepted 
  3350  service Tenure Group II for purposes of Sec.  351.502 and that 
  3351  expiration of a Recent Graduates appointment is not otherwise subject 
  3352  to part 351. Because this final rule replaces the prior excepted-
  3353  service tenure-group structure with the ``excepted service tenure 
  3354  group'' and excludes employees serving a trial period from RIF 
  3355  competition, the current reference to excepted service Tenure Group II 
  3356  is no longer accurate.
  3357      This final rule therefore provides that Recent Graduates are in the 
  3358  excepted service tenure group for purposes of Sec.  351.502 upon 
  3359  completion of a trial period under Sec.  11.3. This amendment 
  3360  harmonizes Sec.  362.306 with the revised definition of ``competing 
  3361  employee'' and the revised coverage and tenure provisions in part 351. 
  3362  It also parallels the rule's treatment of Pathways interns, for whom 
  3363  OPM proposed to remove obsolete RIF language because Pathways 
  3364  participants serving trial periods are not competing employees under 
  3365  the revised part 351 framework. Revising Sec.  362.306(a) applies the 
  3366  same principle to the Recent Graduates Program and prevents confusion 
  3367  caused by obsolete tenure-group terminology.
  3368  
  3369  M. Part 430: Performance Appraisals
  3370  
  3371      OPM is revising Sec.  430.208(e)(4) to conform part 430 to the 
  3372  modified RIF performance-credit framework in part 351. Current Sec.  
  3373  430.208 refers to summary levels as a reference point for assigning 
  3374  additional retention service credit under part 351. Because this rule 
  3375  eliminates the current performance-adjusted service-credit model and 
  3376  replaces it with direct performance-credit values under Sec.  351.503, 
  3377  that reference is no longer accurate.
  3378      The revised provision preserves the role of summary levels and 
  3379  summary-level patterns as the common reference point for describing 
  3380  ratings of record and applying related regulations. Thus, ratings of 
  3381  record assigned under part 430 continue to provide the baseline for 
  3382  calculating performance credit in a RIF. At the same time, the revised 
  3383  language clarifies that enhanced performance values authorized by Sec.  
  3384  351.503 are governed by part 351 and are not constrained by the 
  3385  ordinary summary-level reference in Sec.  430.208.
  3386      Enhanced performance values under Sec.  351.503 do not change the 
  3387  employee's rating of record or alter the part 430 appraisal system. 
  3388  They operate only for RIF retention-standing purposes, and only where 
  3389  part 351 permits such treatment. This clarification ensures that part 
  3390  430 and part 351 operate together: part 430 supplies the rating-of-
  3391  record and summary-level framework, while part 351 governs how those 
  3392  ratings, and any authorized RIF-specific enhancements, are converted 
  3393  into retention-standing credit.
  3394  
  3395  IV. Implementation Considerations
  3396  
  3397      OPM recognizes that agencies that may be conducting RIFs may be 
  3398  impacted by the changes resulting from this rule, particularly where an 
  3399  agency has recently issued RIF notices with RIF effective dates that 
  3400  may occur near the effective date of this rule. To provide clear 
  3401  implementation instructions, OPM is requiring compliance with this 
  3402  final
  3403  
  3404  [[Page 49207]]
  3405  
  3406  rule based on the date the agency issues the RIF notice.
  3407      An agency that issues a RIF notice before September 2, 2026 must 
  3408  process the RIF under the regulations in effect when the notice was 
  3409  issued. An agency that issues a RIF notice on or after September 2, 
  3410  2026 must apply the RIF provisions as amended by this final rule. OPM 
  3411  believes that this implementation approach provides clear and 
  3412  consistent guidance to agencies. It also aligns with the revised 
  3413  regulations, under which the effective date of retention standing is 
  3414  calculated as of the date the employee receives the RIF notice, rather 
  3415  than the RIF effective date (typically 60 days after issuance of the 
  3416  RIF notice).
  3417

I'm checking the preamble against the regulation text, and one reference doesn't line up: the preamble cites Sec. 353.301(b) for the retention protections, but the regulation actually revised 353.301(a), along with 353.209(a). Another passage at 3319 correctly gives 353.301(a), so the mismatch is isolated to this one spot.

I'm now working through the rest of the preamble against the part 330 text. The finalizing-probationary-appointment exception looks consistent with the 330.609 and 330.707 additions. I'll also confirm the Pathways termination and 362.205 removal, the 362.306(a) tenure group, and the Sept 2 date, then read the 330 provisions around 330.213 and 330.404 to see whether the preamble covers the veterans' points and preference-eligible displacement.

content.text:
I'm checking the regulation text against the preamble, and I've spotted an inconsistency: §330.213(c)(1) says "does not principally rely" on an automated self-assessment, while §330.202 says "does not consist solely of, or principally rely" on it, and the preamble puts it differently again. I'm also noting that §330.202(5)(iv) has been corrected, and I need to look at the correction text for §330.602 next.

I'm confirming the correction text for §330.602, where the pre-correction paragraph (1) held only the introductory language and the correction removed items (i) and (ii). I'm also noting what that paragraph read on September 10, before the correction. Next I'll turn to the remaining questions and set the budget, starting with the appeals rule's regulatory text.

content.text:
I'm checking the Board's rule for an internal inconsistency on question 14(iii). The dates section says it won't apply to newly filed cases tied to agency actions taken before OPM's rulemakings take effect, while Section B keys RIF appeals to when the agency's notice was issued, and the closing line keys them to when the RIF effective date falls.

I'm weighing a few smaller points about the Foreign Service carve-out and whether OPM's jurisdiction language squares with the Board's. I also see that "pending as of Sept 2" may not matter much, since those appeals relate to earlier notices anyway. The real mismatch is the scenario where notice goes out August 31 and separation falls October 30: OPM's rule keys to the notice, but the Board's sentence keys to the effective date.

I'm checking which documents bear on Q7(a): the MSPB's DATES section and its notice-date language point to MSPB hearing these appeals, but there's a conflicting sentence I should flag. Next I'll read the OPM summary of changes in the final rule and compare it against the proposed appeals regulatory text.

[2026-15666: lines 83-344 of 4700, FR page 49230]
    83  DATES: Effective September 2, 2026. This final rule applies only to a 
    84  RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF 
    85  notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026.
    86  
    87  FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Aaron Gottesman, Senior Advisor to the 
    88  Director, by email at [email protected] or by phone at 
    89  (202) 606-7400.
    90  
    91  SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: OPM is issuing this final rule to modernize 
    92  the administrative process for appeals by employees who are furloughed 
    93  for more than 30 days, separated, or demoted by a reduction-in-force 
    94  action under 5 CFR part 351. Congress charged OPM with prescribing 
    95  regulations governing the release of competing employees in a RIF, and 
    96  OPM has historically implemented RIF appeal procedures through 
    97  regulation. This final rule revises that regulatory framework by 
    98  replacing the prior MSPB forum for future non-SES RIF appeals with a 
    99  uniform OPM-administered process. The rule does not alter agencies' 
   100  responsibility to determine their workforce needs or whether a RIF is 
   101  necessary. By requiring a complete RIF-specific agency record, 
   102  permitting an appellant reply, authorizing additional information, 
   103  audits, investigations, and hearings when necessary and efficient, and 
   104  preserving collateral statutory remedies, the final rule provides 
   105  meaningful administrative review while reducing delay, fragmentation, 
   106  and unnecessary litigation burden.
   107  
   108  I. Digest of Public Comments and Summary of Changes From the Proposed 
   109  Rule
   110  
   111      In response to the proposed rule, OPM received 1,252 comments 
   112  during the 30-day public comment period from a variety of individuals, 
   113  including current and former civil servants, members of Congress, as 
   114  well as organizations, including local and national unions and Federal 
   115  agencies. Of the 1,252 comments, 1,251 were posted on 
   116  www.regulations.gov, and one was not posted because it contained vulgar 
   117  language unrelated to the rulemaking in question. At the conclusion of 
   118  the public comment period, OPM reviewed and analyzed the comments. In 
   119  general, the comments ranged from ardent support of the proposed 
   120  regulation to categorical rejection of it. Less than 1 percent of the 
   121  overall comments were supportive, neutral, or mixed, and 99 percent 
   122  opposed the proposed regulation.
   123      OPM found many of the comments helpful. OPM has revised the final 
   124  rule to clarify, narrow, or supplement the proposed RIF appeal 
   125  procedures in response to comments, including comments concerning 
   126  burden of proof, access to the agency record, information asymmetry, 
   127  due process, neutrality, hearings, protective orders, collective 
   128  bargaining, and public disclosure. In response to those comments, the 
   129  final rule adds more precise appeal standards, a detailed RIF-specific 
   130  agency-record requirement, disclosure and privilege protections, 
   131  stronger adjudicator-separation and ex parte safeguards, narrower e-
   132  filing sanctions, more flexible reply rules, and more carefully 
   133  tailored protective order and public posting provisions. The revisions 
   134  are summarized below.
   135      Clarifying appealable actions. The final text clarifies the 
   136  appealable actions set forth in Sec.  351.901(a). The proposal allowed 
   137  an employee ``who has been the subject of a reduction-in-force action'' 
   138  to appeal an action taken under part 351. The final text specifies that 
   139  only an employee furloughed for more than 30 days, separated, or 
   140  demoted by a RIF action taken under part 351 may appeal that action to 
   141  OPM.
   142      Revising the merits standard. The final text replaces the proposed 
   143  ``would not have suffered the same or another RIF action'' standard in 
   144  Sec.  351.901(b) with a more precise two-part merits showing: the 
   145  appellant must prove that the agency failed to comply with an 
   146  applicable statute or OPM regulation governing RIF actions under part 
   147  351, and the failure prejudiced the appellant by causing the appealed 
   148  action or the loss of a materially more favorable outcome. This is 
   149  clearer and better focused on prejudicial RIF-compliance error.
   150      Revising exclusivity language. The final text continues to provide 
   151  that part 351 procedures are the sole and exclusive means of appealing 
   152  a RIF action, and adds that RIFs and matters related to the appeals of 
   153  RIFs cannot be raised in grievance procedures or challenged through 
   154  grievance arbitration, while expressly preserving collateral matters 
   155  within the independent jurisdiction of Equal Employment Opportunity 
   156  Commission (EEOC), Inspectors General, MSPB, Department of Labor 
   157  Veterans' Employment and Training Service (DOL VETS), and the Office of 
   158  Special Counsel (OSC). The final text also retains the no-judicial-
   159  review provision.
   160      Updating filing-system language. The final text replaces the 
   161  proposed placeholder for the electronic filing system with a reference 
   162  to the system identified on OPM's website. It also replaces 
   163  ``statements, evidence, or documents'' with ``pleadings, evidence, or 
   164  documents,'' better aligning the filing provision with adjudicatory 
   165  terminology.
   166      Clarifying filing deadlines. The final text changes the filing 
   167  deadline from 11:59 p.m. Eastern Standard Time to 11:59 p.m. Eastern 
   168  Time, avoiding confusion during daylight saving time. It also 
   169  consolidates the untimely-filing rule in Sec.  351.902(b)(2) and 
   170  provides that good-cause determinations are within OPM's sole and 
   171  exclusive discretion.
   172      Adding a limited tolling rule for collateral matters. The final 
   173  text adds Sec.  351.902(b)(3), which permits an employee who timely 
   174  filed a collateral matter within the independent jurisdiction of an 
   175  entity identified in Sec.  351.901(c) to file a RIF appeal within 30 
   176  calendar days after the final decision on that matter, where that 
   177  decision materially affects the employee's retention standing, order of 
   178  release, assignment rights, or other rights under part 351. The final 
   179  text provides that a decision is final for this purpose when it is no 
   180  longer subject to further administrative review and that OPM 
   181  determines, in its sole and exclusive discretion, whether the decision 
   182  materially affects the employee's rights.
   183      Requiring filing-information detail in the RIF notice. The final 
   184  text amends Sec.  351.802(a)(6) to require the specific RIF notice to 
   185  state, in addition to the employee's right to appeal to OPM, the
   186  
   187  [[Page 49231]]
   188  
   189  time limit for filing an appeal under Sec.  351.902(b) and the 
   190  electronic filing system through which an appeal must be filed.
   191      Narrowing e-filing enforcement. The final text narrows the proposed 
   192  e-filing enforcement provisions. Rather than authorizing broader orders 
   193  regulating filing methods, sanctions, misuse, or termination of e-filer 
   194  participation, the final text provides that OPM may strike a document 
   195  when an e-filer repeatedly fails to follow filing instructions after a 
   196  show-cause order. The final text also removes the proposed statement 
   197  that withdrawal from e-filing may preclude future re-registration and 
   198  clarifies that withdrawal of e-filing registration is not good cause 
   199  for staying a case.
   200      Simplifying initial-appeal information. The final text simplifies 
   201  the contact-information requirements in Sec.  351.903(a) by replacing 
   202  ``legal name, best address'' with ``name, address.'' The core 
   203  requirement remains unchanged: the appeal must be written, state the 
   204  basis for the appeal, identify the appellant and any representative, 
   205  and include supporting documentation.
   206      Defining the agency record. The final text adds a RIF-specific 
   207  minimum agency-record requirement to Sec.  351.903(b). The proposal 
   208  required the agency response to include the agency record but did not 
   209  define its contents. The final text specifies that the agency record 
   210  includes, at a minimum, the RIF notice and effective-date documents, 
   211  documents supporting the RIF reason, coverage and appointment records, 
   212  competitive-area and competitive-level records, retention-register and 
   213  retention-standing records, order-of-release records, assignment-rights 
   214  records, special RIF-circumstance records, and a certification that the 
   215  complete agency record has been produced.
   216      Distinguishing production to OPM from service on the appellant. The 
   217  final text requires the agency to produce the complete agency record to 
   218  OPM while serving the appellant with the agency record subject to 
   219  legally required limits. The agency may redact or withhold information 
   220  from the appellant's copy only to the extent necessary to comply with 
   221  the Privacy Act, applicable legal privileges, classified-information or 
   222  national-security requirements, OPM protective orders, or other 
   223  disclosure limits required by law.
   224      Allowing limited new matters in reply. The final text revises Sec.  
   225  351.903(c) to permit an appellant's reply to raise a new allegation of 
   226  error if the basis for that allegation rests on information first 
   227  disclosed in the agency response or if OPM grants leave for good cause.
   228      Adding disclosure limits for inspection and service. The final text 
   229  makes inspection of OPM's appellate record and service of documents 
   230  subject to the Privacy Act, applicable legal privileges, classified-
   231  information or national-security requirements, OPM protective orders, 
   232  and other applicable disclosure limits required by law. The proposal 
   233  allowed inspection and required service but did not include the same 
   234  express disclosure limitations.
   235      Reorganizing representative provisions. The final text reorganizes 
   236  Sec.  351.904 into separate paragraphs addressing designation of a 
   237  representative, Federal employee representatives and restrictions on 
   238  official time and reimbursement, and disallowance of representatives. 
   239  The final text also narrows the grounds for disallowing a 
   240  representative. Because a Federal employee representative may not 
   241  perform representational functions while in a duty status, the final 
   242  text does not adopt the proposed additional grounds for disallowance 
   243  based on the priority needs of the Government or unreasonable costs to 
   244  the Government; OPM or the responsible agency may disallow an 
   245  employee's choice of representative only where the representative is an 
   246  employee of the responsible agency or OPM and the representative's 
   247  activities would cause a conflict of interest or position. The 
   248  remaining changes are primarily organizational and clarifying.
   249      Adding adjudicator-separation and ex parte safeguards. The final 
   250  text adds safeguards in Sec.  351.905(a) requiring OPM adjudicators to 
   251  be insulated from officials who participated personally and 
   252  substantially in the challenged action or provided case-specific 
   253  advice. It also prohibits adjudicators from considering material ex 
   254  parte communications on the merits and requires any such communication 
   255  to be summarized in the record with an opportunity for party response, 
   256  unless disclosure is prohibited by law.
   257      Clarifying OPM employee appeals. The final text clarifies that an 
   258  administrative law judge (ALJ) assigned to adjudicate an OPM employee's 
   259  appeal will issue an initial decision. It also adds material factual 
   260  error affecting the outcome as a ground on which OPM may disturb the 
   261  ALJ's decision and clarifies that assigning an ALJ does not make 5 
   262  U.S.C. 554, 556, or 557 applicable unless independently required by law 
   263  or expressly incorporated.
   264      Tightening audits and investigations. The final text narrows the 
   265  standard for OPM audits or investigations. The proposal allowed OPM to 
   266  conduct an audit or investigation when the ``interest of justice'' 
   267  would be served. The final text requires OPM to determine that the 
   268  existing record is insufficient to resolve a material issue within 
   269  OPM's jurisdiction and that the audit or investigation is reasonably 
   270  likely to produce material information. The final text also provides 
   271  that representatives may not participate in an audit or investigation 
   272  unless OPM specifically requests it.
   273      Removing a separate ascertainment sanction. The final text removes 
   274  the proposed separate paragraph authorizing sanctions for failure to 
   275  participate in ascertainment of facts and renumbers the initial-
   276  decision and remedies provisions.
   277      Refining protective-order authority. The final text revises Sec.  
   278  351.906(a). The proposal focused on harassing communications and use of 
   279  appeal information for unrelated purposes. The final text authorizes 
   280  protective orders or cease-and-desist directives to protect the 
   281  integrity of the adjudicatory process and to prevent threats, 
   282  intimidation, targeted harassment, improper witness contact, disclosure 
   283  of protected personal information, or misuse of nonpublic information 
   284  obtained through the appeal. It also requires protective orders to be 
   285  no broader than reasonably necessary and not to restrict lawful 
   286  communications protected by law.
   287      Clarifying OPM-initiated reconsideration. The final text clarifies 
   288  in Sec.  351.907(a) that OPM may reopen and reconsider an initial 
   289  decision either upon request of a party or on its own initiative. The 
   290  proposal allowed party-requested reconsideration, while Director sua 
   291  sponte review was addressed separately.
   292      Clarifying Director review. The final text revises Sec.  351.908 to 
   293  preserve the Director's sua sponte authority to reopen and reconsider a 
   294  nonfinal initial decision or reopened and reconsidered decision, while 
   295  identifying nonexclusive considerations that may guide that review. The 
   296  proposal gave the Director broad discretion to reopen and reconsider 
   297  any nonfinal decision. The final text clarifies that the Director may 
   298  consider whether the decision contains clear legal error, rests on an 
   299  erroneous material factual finding, involves an issue of exceptional 
   300  importance, affects governmentwide civil service administration, 
   301  conflicts with another OPM decision, or otherwise warrants review. It 
   302  also clarifies that Sec.  351.908 does not create a party right to 
   303  request Director review and that, upon reopening, the Director may take 
   304  any action available under Sec.  351.907(c).
   305  
   306  [[Page 49232]]
   307  
   308      Revising finality of initial decisions. The final text revises 
   309  Sec.  351.909 so that an initial decision becomes final 30 calendar 
   310  days after issuance unless, before that time, a party timely requests 
   311  reopening and reconsideration under Sec.  351.907 or the Director 
   312  reopens the decision under Sec.  351.908. A timely request suspends 
   313  finality: if OPM denies or dismisses the request without reopening the 
   314  initial decision, the initial decision becomes final 30 calendar days 
   315  after issuance of the denial or dismissal unless the Director reopens 
   316  it before that time, and if OPM grants the request, the reopened and 
   317  reconsidered decision becomes final 30 calendar days after issuance 
   318  unless the Director reopens that decision before that time. An untimely 
   319  request does not suspend or otherwise affect finality. The final text 
   320  also clarifies that a decision by the Director that disposes of the 
   321  appeal is final and effective upon issuance and that, if the Director 
   322  remands the appeal or directs further proceedings, any resulting 
   323  decision becomes final under Sec.  351.909. These changes conform 
   324  finality to the reconsideration and Director-review provisions of the 
   325  final rule.
   326      Adding public-posting disclosure limits. The final text adds 
   327  express legal limits on public posting of final merits decisions, 
   328  including requirements protecting privacy, privileged information, 
   329  protected personnel information, law-enforcement-sensitive information, 
   330  and other information that may not lawfully be disclosed. It also 
   331  clarifies that final merits decisions not publicly posted because of 
   332  such legal limits must be made available upon request to the Federal 
   333  employee or former Federal employee involved in a proceeding under this 
   334  subpart, his or her representative selected pursuant to Sec.  351.904, 
   335  or a representative of the Federal agency or office involved in the 
   336  proceeding who has a need to know.
   337      OPM is finalizing the RIF appeals rule as amended. After 
   338  considering the comments, OPM concludes that the final rule, as 
   339  amended, better balances timely adjudication, governmentwide 
   340  consistency, employee access to meaningful administrative review, and 
   341  agencies' need for finality in workforce restructuring than the current 
   342  MSPB appeal process for non-SES RIFs.
   343  
   344  II. Background

I'm finishing the check on the untimely filing rule's citation, and now I'm moving on to find the proposed appeals rule text in document 2026-02576 so I can compare it against the summary for any changes it doesn't acknowledge.

  1909  
  1910      (a) Right of appeal. An employee who has been the subject of a 
  1911  reduction-in-force action may appeal an action taken under this part to 
  1912  the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).
  1913      (b) Burden of Proof. The employee (i.e., appellant) bears the

  1921  action.
  1922      (c) Exclusive appeal procedure. The procedures in this part are the 
  1923  sole and exclusive means of appealing any reduction-in-force action, 
  1924  and shall supersede any appeal procedures found in agency policies or 
  1925  collective bargaining agreements, but they do not otherwise preclude an 
  1926  employee from filing a complaint, appeal, or other matter within the 
  1927  jurisdiction of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Federal 
  1928  Labor Relations Authority, an Inspector General, Merit Systems 
  1929  Protection Board, the Department of Labor Veterans' Employment and 
  1930  Training Service, or the Office of Special Counsel. A party cannot 
  1931  obtain judicial review of a decision under this part.
  1932  
  1933  
  1934  Sec.  351.902  Procedures for submitting appeals.
  1935  
  1936      (a) Filing an appeal. A party, or his or her authorized 
  1937  representative, seeking to file an initial appeal or reconsideration of 
  1938  an initial appeal under this part must utilize the electronic filing 
  1939  (e-filing) system available at [URL TBD]. Unless a party demonstrates 
  1940  good cause and seeks approval from OPM, OPM will not accept any 
  1941  statements, evidence, or documents via electronic mail or postal mail.
  1942      (b) Time limits. An employee may submit an appeal of a reduction in 
  1943  force action within 30 calendar days from the effective date of the 
  1944  action. An appeal is deemed timely when it is electronically filed by 
  1945  11:59 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on the 30th calendar day after the 
  1946  effective date of the action.
  1947      (1) In computing the number of days allowed for filing an appeal, 
  1948  the first day counted is the day after the effective date of an Agency 
  1949  action. If the date that ordinarily would be the last day for filing 
  1950  falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday, the filing period will 
  1951  include the first workday after that date.
  1952      (2) If an employee does not submit an appeal within the time set by 
  1953  this section, the appeal will be dismissed as untimely filed unless the 
  1954  employee demonstrates good cause for an untimely appeal.
  1955      (3) The determination of good cause will be in the sole and 
  1956  exclusive discretion of OPM.
  1957      (c) E-filing procedures.
  1958      (1) All parties and their representatives to an appeal or 
  1959  reconsideration must register as instructed by OPM on its e-filing 
  1960  system using a unique email address.
  1961      (2) Registration as an e-filer constitutes consent to accept 
  1962  electronic service of pleadings, evidence, notices, orders, and other 
  1963  documents filed by other e-filers or issued by OPM. No party may 
  1964  electronically file any document with OPM or access an appeal or 
  1965  reconsideration of an appeal unless registered as an e-filer.
  1966      (3) All notices, orders, decisions, and other documents issued by 
  1967  OPM, as well as all documents filed by parties, will be made available 
  1968  for viewing and downloading at OPM's electronic filing system. Access 
  1969  to documents is limited to the parties and their representatives who 
  1970  are registered e-filers in the cases in which they were filed.
  1971      (4) All parties and their representatives must follow the 
  1972  instructions on OPM's website for properly filing all pleadings, 
  1973  evidence, and other documents. OPM may issue orders regulating the 
  1974  method and form of submissions and sanctions for noncompliance, 
  1975  including ordering any party or authorized individual to cease 
  1976  participation as an e-filer in circumstances that constitute a misuse 
  1977  of the system or a failure to comply with law, rule, regulations, or 
  1978  policy governing the use of a U.S. government information system.
  1979      (5) Each e-filer must promptly update their profile in OPM's 
  1980  electronic filing system and notify OPM and other parties of any change 
  1981  in their best address, telephone number, or email address by filing a 
  1982  pleading in each pending case with which they are associated. E-filers 
  1983  are responsible for monitoring case activity regularly in OPM's 
  1984  electronic filing system to ensure that they have received all case-
  1985  related documents.
  1986      (6) A party or representative may withdraw their registration as an 
  1987  e-filer pursuant to the requirements posted on OPM's website. 
  1988  Withdrawing registration in OPM's e-filing system means that, effective 
  1989  upon OPM's processing of a proper withdrawal, pleadings, evidence, 
  1990  orders, and other documents filed by a party or party's representative 
  1991  and OPM will no longer be served on that person electronically and that 
  1992  person will no longer have electronic access to their case records 
  1993  through OPM's e-filing system. OPM may still process an appeal or 
  1994  request for reconsideration after a party withdraws as an e-filer. 
  1995  Withdrawal as a party or party's representative will not be considered 
  1996  good cause for staying a case. As the e-file system is the only 
  1997  accepted method for filing an appeal, a withdrawal of registration as 
  1998  an e-filer may preclude future re-registering as an e-filer.
  1999      (7) OPM, in its sole and exclusive discretion, may exempt a party 
  2000  or representative from registering as an e-filer for good cause. A 
  2001  party or representative must promptly contact OPM as instructed on 
  2002  OPM's website to request an exemption from the e-filing requirements in 
  2003  this part. OPM will not find good cause for failing to timely file an 
  2004  appeal or seek reconsideration if the party or representative fails to 
  2005  contact OPM to request an exemption before any deadline to appeal or 
  2006  seek reconsideration.
  2007      (8) Documents filed in OPM's e-filing system are deemed received on 
  2008  the date of the electronic submission.

  2012  
  2013      (a) Initial appeal. An employee's appeal shall be in writing and 
  2014  must state the basis of the employee's appeal; and the legal name, best 
  2015  address, and email address or phone number of the appellant and 
  2016  appellant's representative, if any; and must include any documentation 
  2017  supporting the appellant's appeal.
  2018      (b) Agency response. The agency response to an appeal must be filed 
  2019  within 30 calendar days of the initial appeal; contain the name of the 
  2020  appellant and of the agency whose action the appellant is appealing; a 
  2021  statement identifying the agency action taken against the appellant and 
  2022  stating the reasons for taking the action; all documents contained in 
  2023  the agency record of the action; designation of and signature by the 
  2024  authorized agency representative; and any other documents or responses 
  2025  requested by OPM. The agency's 30 days to respond begins upon service 
  2026  of the appeal.

  2028  [[Page 5876]]
  2029  
  2030      (c) Reply. The employee may file a reply to the agency response to 
  2031  an initial appeal within 15 calendar days of the agency response. The 
  2032  reply may only address the factual and legal issues raised by the 
  2033  agency in response to the initial appeal. The reply may not raise new 
  2034  allegations of error.
  2035      (d) Inspection of OPM's appellate record. The employee, an 
  2036  employee's representative, and the agency will be permitted to inspect 
  2037  OPM's appellate record on request.
  2038      (e) Service of Documents. The employee, employee's representative, 
  2039  and agency will serve on each other copies of any and all information 
  2040  submitted to OPM with respect to an appeal. Such information must be 
  2041  served on all other parties at the same time the information is 
  2042  submitted to OPM and must be accompanied by a certificate of service 
  2043  stating how and when service was made.
  2044      (f) Untimely Filings. Untimely filings may be accepted upon a 
  2045  party's showing of good cause at the sole and exclusive discretion of 
  2046  OPM.

  2049  Sec.  351.904  Employee representatives.
  2050  
  2051      An employee may select a representative of his or her choice to 
  2052  assist in the preparation and presentation of an appeal, provided that 
  2053  the employee submits his or her designation of representative in 
  2054  writing related to the specific appeal. If the selected representative 
  2055  is a Federal employee, the representative may not perform such 
  2056  representational functions while in a duty status (including while on 
  2057  official time under 5 U.S.C. 7131), nor may the representative claim 
  2058  agency reimbursement for any expenses incurred while performing such 
  2059  representational function. OPM or the responsible agency may, in its 
  2060  sole and exclusive discretion, disallow an employee's choice of 
  2061  representative when the representative is an employee of the 
  2062  responsible agency or OPM and his or her activities as a representative 
  2063  would cause a conflict of interest or position; that employee cannot be 
  2064  released from his or her official duties because of the priority needs 
  2065  of the Government; or that employee's release would give rise to 
  2066  unreasonable costs to the Government.
  2067  
  2068  
  2069  Sec.  351.905  Adjudication of appeals.
  2070  
  2071      (a) Appeals by non-OPM employees. OPM will assign personnel to 
  2072  adjudicate an appeal under this subpart by an employee of an agency 
  2073  other than OPM. However, no OPM employee may be assigned to adjudicate 
  2074  an appeal if the employee has a relationship with the appellant 
  2075  employee or, during the preceding two years, that person was an 
  2076  employee of the agency that is a party to the action to be assigned, or 
  2077  the employee was subject to, an action covered under this part. When 
  2078  necessary, OPM may appoint an administrative law judge to preside over 
  2079  the adjudication of an appeal.
  2080      (b) Appeals by OPM employees. OPM will assign an administrative law 
  2081  judge to adjudicate an appeal under this subpart by an OPM employee. To 
  2082  insulate the adjudication of its own employees' appeals from agency 
  2083  involvement, OPM will not disturb initial decisions in those cases 
  2084  unless a party shows that there has been harmful procedural 
  2085  irregularity in the proceedings before the administrative law judge or 
  2086  a clear error of law. For these purposes, the term harmful procedural 
  2087  irregularity means an irregularity in the application of procedures was 
  2088  likely to have caused the administrative law judge to reach a 
  2089  conclusion different from the one he or she would have reached in the 
  2090  absence or cure of the irregularity.
  2091      (c) Ascertainment of facts. OPM may audit or investigate an 
  2092  agency's reduction in force action in the course of adjudicating an 
  2093  appeal if it determines, in its sole and exclusive discretion, the 
  2094  interest of justice is served by such an audit or investigation. The 
  2095  review of an agency action will be based solely on the developed 
  2096  written record unless OPM determines that a hearing or any other 
  2097  appropriate action is necessary and efficient to resolve an appeal and 
  2098  directs the parties to participate in such hearing or comply with such 
  2099  action. For purposes of this section, the term necessary and efficient 
  2100  means circumstances in which the written record is insufficiently 
  2101  developed to make a determination regarding one or more facts material 
  2102  to the outcome of the appeal, or where there is a disputed issue of 
  2103  witness credibility that is material to the outcome of the appeal. 
  2104  Where an investigation or audit is conducted, OPM will:
  2105      (1) Inform the employee, the employee's representative, and the 
  2106  agency of an investigation or audit; and
  2107      (2) Provide the employee, the employee's representative, and the 
  2108  agency with the results of an investigation or audit, and a reasonable 
  2109  opportunity to submit arguments or additional information to support 
  2110  their positions.
  2111      (d) Failure to participate in ascertainment of facts. If a party 
  2112  fails to participate in an audit or investigation pursuant to 
  2113  351.905(c), OPM may, except when prohibited by law, impose any sanction 
  2114  listed at 351.906(b)(1)-(3).
  2115      (e) Initial decision. OPM will notify the employee, employee's 
  2116  representative, and agency in writing of its decision.
  2117      (f) Remedies. (1) If the employee is the prevailing party, OPM will 
  2118  order relief including correction of the personnel action and any back 
  2119  pay, interest, and reasonable attorney fees consistent with subpart H 
  2120  of part 550 of this chapter. The employee as a prevailing party is not 
  2121  entitled to compensatory damages or other relief not authorized under 5 
  2122  U.S.C. 5596(b).
  2123      (2) If the agency timely requests reconsideration of an initial 
  2124  decision or OPM reopens and reconsiders an initial decision, the agency 
  2125  must continue to provide the relief ordered unless OPM issues an order 
  2126  staying any such relief. No such stay may be ordered that would deprive 
  2127  pay and benefits to the employee while the initial decision is pending 
  2128  reconsideration.
  2129  
  2130  
  2131  Sec.  351.906  Sanctions and protective orders.
  2132  
  2133      (a) Cease-and-desist directive. OPM may issue a directive to a 
  2134  party to prevent or to cease-and-desist harassing communications (or 
  2135  communications which could reasonably be foreseen to lead to 
  2136  harassment) with or about any individual, or to prohibit a party from 
  2137  using any information related to the appeal for any purpose whatsoever 
  2138  unrelated to the adjudication of the appeal. OPM may do this sua 
  2139  sponte, or at the request of a party, preemptively or at any juncture 
  2140  in the appeal process. A party requesting OPM to issue a protective 
  2141  order or cease-and-desist should file such request using the e-filing 
  2142  procedures proscribed at Sec.  351.902(c), and must include statement 
  2143  of reasons justifying the request, together with any relevant 
  2144  documentary evidence.
  2145      (b) Failure to comply with an OPM directive. When a party to an 
  2146  appeal fails to comply with a directive issued under paragraph (a), OPM 
  2147  shall, except when prohibited by law:
  2148      (1) Draw all inferences in opposition to the noncompliant party 
  2149  with regard to the appeal in question;
  2150      (2) Prohibit the noncompliant party from introducing evidence, or 
  2151  additional evidence, concerning the appeal, or otherwise relying on the 
  2152  record; or
  2153      (3) Eliminate from consideration any appropriate part of the 
  2154  filings or other submissions of the noncompliant party.
  2155  
  2156  
  2157  Sec.  351.907  Reconsideration of an initial decision.
  2158  
  2159      (a) Upon a request from either party to the dispute, OPM may, in 
  2160  its sole and
  2161  
  2162  [[Page 5877]]
  2163  
  2164  exclusive discretion, reopen and reconsider an initial decision issued 
  2165  under this subpart. An employee, the employee's representative, or the 
  2166  agency may request reopening and reconsideration of an initial decision 
  2167  within 30 calendar days from issuance of the initial decision. The 
  2168  request to reopen and reconsider must be filed in the same manner as an 
  2169  initial appeal.
  2170      (b) Grounds for which OPM may grant a request for reconsideration 
  2171  are:
  2172      (1) The initial decision contains erroneous findings of material 
  2173  fact sufficient to warrant an outcome different from that of the 
  2174  initial decision;
  2175      (2) The initial decision is based on an erroneous interpretation of 
  2176  statute or regulation or the erroneous application of the law to the 
  2177  facts of the case. The party must explain how the error affected the 
  2178  outcome of the case;
  2179      (3) New and material evidence or legal argument is available that, 
  2180  despite the party's due diligence, was not available when the record 
  2181  closed. To constitute new evidence, the information contained in the 
  2182  documents, not just the documents themselves, must have been 
  2183  unavailable despite due diligence when the record closed; or
  2184      (4) OPM finds good cause to reconsider an appeal.
  2185      (c) In any case that is reopened or reviewed, OPM may:
  2186      (1) Issue a reopened and reconsidered decision (``R&R decision'') 
  2187  that affirms, reverses, modifies, vacates, or otherwise decides the 
  2188  case, in whole or in part;
  2189      (2) Require the parties to submit argument and evidence;
  2190      (3) Take any other action necessary for final disposition of the 
  2191  case; and
  2192      (4) Issue an order with a date for compliance with the R&R 
  2193  decision.
  2194      (d) There is no further right of administrative appeal from the R&R 
  2195  decision.
  2196  
  2197  
  2198  Sec.  351.908   Review by the OPM Director.
  2199  
  2200      The Director may, at his or her discretion, sua sponte, reopen and 
  2201  reconsider any appeal in which OPM has issued a decision that has not 
  2202  yet become final.
  2203  
  2204  
  2205  Sec.  351.909  Final decision.
  2206  
  2207      (a) The initial decision becomes the final decision of OPM if a 
  2208  party does not request OPM to reopen or reconsider the initial decision 
  2209  within 30 calendar days from the date of the initial decision.
  2210      (b) A R&R decision pursuant to Sec.  351.907 becomes OPM's final 
  2211  decision if the OPM Director does not reopen the decision pursuant to 
  2212  Sec.  351.908 within 30 calendar days from the date on which the R&R 
  2213  decision was issued.
  2214      (c) A decision by the Director pursuant to Sec.  351.908 is the

content.text:
I'm checking the Q14 (ii) unacknowledged changes. In 351.901(c), the proposed rule named the Federal Labor Relations Authority among the entities with independent jurisdiction, but the final rule's list drops it. The summary doesn't mention that removal.

I'm going through the rest of the unacknowledged changes: the "supersede" language on the appeal procedures in 351.901(c) was removed and replaced with a grievance bar, which the summary only partly covers. I'm also noting the shift from "appeal" to "written appeal" in 351.901(b)(1), the dropped MSPB notice cross-reference in 351.802(a)(6), the changed authority citations, and the "initial appeal" to "initial decision" wording in 351.902(a).

I'm going through the remaining final-rule changes in 351.902 and 351.903: the exemption added to 351.902(c)(2) for good cause, the drop of "best" from the address requirement in (c)(5), and the shift in 351.903(b)(1) from a 30-day window after the initial appeal to a window running after service. I'm also checking 351.905, where "any other appropriate action" and the direction to participate were removed from (c), and the summary doesn't acknowledge either.

I'm checking the remaining unacknowledged changes in 351.906: the "shall" in (b) became "may," which the summary doesn't mention, and a new sanctions-scope paragraph in (c) isn't covered there either. Item 18 on 351.904 is already acknowledged, so I can set it aside.

I'm going through the last few items in the list: the 351.905(b) change that adds "a material factual error," which I'll note as covered, and the remaining entries I've already checked against the summary.

I'm now checking the preamble against the regulation text on a few points. The summary says the rule replaces the prior MSPB forum for future non-SES RIF appeals, but the regulation has no SES carve-out, so I'll search the preamble for "SES" to see whether that limit is stated anywhere. I also want to compare the preamble's description of the filing deadline, reply restrictions, and disallowance language against the final text.

I'm going to scan the preamble for mentions of SES, grievance procedures, judicial review, and the specific deadline lengths, to check whether the summary's claims hold up against the text.

I'm looking at (c)(10), which covers administrative leave for a RIF between the notice and separation when the agency decides it's in the best interests. Consent isn't required, and unlike (c)(9) and (c)(11) it doesn't carry the "subject to Governmentwide limits" parenthetical. The relevant cap is in the policy template: 12 weeks per instance for workforce realignment, which I'm checking against the preamble on page 65935.

I'm checking whether the 12-week workforce realignment limit covers the RIF notice period, and counting the paid leave from October 26 to December 18, which comes to about 7.5 weeks. I also notice the rule doesn't take effect until November 18, 2026, so the adopted text wasn't in force when those dates fell.

I'm checking whether the 12-week workforce realignment cap applies to RIF notice periods under (c)(10), since that paragraph doesn't carry the governmentwide-limits parenthetical, and I'll flag that as unresolved. I also want to confirm the effective date and check the other Federal Register documents for any effect on Part 351.

content.text:
I'm comparing the proposed and final versions of the rule, starting with the 351.202(d) heading, which was reorganized to define who counts as a "competing employee." I'm also checking (d)(3), where the final version drops the blanket exclusion from this part and instead says those employees aren't required to determine retention standing, apply 351.601, or use assignment rights.

I'm now going through the rest of the differences, starting with the (d)(1)(ii) and (d)(2)(i) trial-period language, where the "as of" date reference was dropped. Then I'm checking the (d)(2)(iii) change that narrows the appointment types to temporary appointments under subpart D, which bears on the term-appointment scenario.

Next I'm going through the 351.503 changes, but that part is long, so I'll skip it for now. After that I'll read sections 504 through 506, then 601 through 608, 701 and 702, and 802, along with Parts 353 and 362.

content.text:
I'm comparing the proposed and final versions of the rule, and so far I've noted that 351.504(a) changes "should" to "must" in three places. I also see that the cross-reference in 351.505(b)(2) moved from 351.503(b) to 351.504(b), which counts as a real change. Next I'm checking how the singular wording in 351.506(c)(1) differs from the plural phrasing in the proposal.

I'm going through the remaining differences in this rule, including 351.506(d), which adds language about access under another statute and which the preamble acknowledges, and 351.507(b), where "this paragraph (b)" becomes "these provisions." Next I'll check sections 601 through 608 and 701, 702, 802, 353, and 362 in the later part of the document.

I'm comparing the 351.604 and 351.606(a) sections against the final rule, noting that 351.604's furlough amendment was dropped and that 351.606(a)'s cross-reference changed from 351.209(b) to 353.209(b). Now I'm moving on to 351.605.

I'm checking the 351.605 wording against the final rule: the paragraph reference and the notice placement differ only in wording and ordering, and the RIF-competition exclusion matches. 351.605(b) is the same in both versions, and the assignment-rights phrasing differs only slightly. 351.602 is unchanged. Next I'll search the proposed 608 text for the stand-alone and day-count language to compare it with the final rule.
